retirement:earlyend: Own-terms expiry on the stated date, recorded per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling as the stated date inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading (the exemption ends when that day begins) is one day earlier and is stated here for the human reviewer. The person's death, resignation or separation before the stated date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an earlier termination of the order; no held record shows any such event. A later 'further exemption' of the same person signed before this order's stated date is a new, overlapping grant that neither revokes nor shortens this order's term (it recites this order and adds a later end date), so it is recorded as a later event, not as an earlier ending. No later order amends, revokes or extends this order before its stated date (see the search). The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act.
retirement:indep: The order contains a single operative command: the time-limited exemption of the named person (or persons) from section 204 and their continuance in the service until the stated date. The recital of the statute, the quotation of its proviso and the identification of the employee, age and position are not independent commands. No retained independent command survives the stated term.
retirement:inventory: Single-clause inventory confirmed on the held transcription: the clause span holds the whole operative text (quoted statutory proviso, the 'Whereas the public interest requires' identification and the 'Now, Therefore ... I do hereby exempt ... until' command). The machine span starts after the first recital line ('Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 ... provides:'), which is a citation of authority and not an operative command; the inventory is complete as to commands. The transcription is the American Presidency Project text, a provisional working text under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.
retirement:savings: Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects of the person's continued employment; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term. A later 'further' exemption of the same person is a new grant under the statute, not a savings clause of this order, and the person's employment after the stated date rests on that later order, not on this one.
retirement:search: Searches judged adequate for this one-person, fixed-term exemption: the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude any current-law reference; the OFR catalog search covers 1937 onward only (coverage warning for the pre-1937 members, and it does report the 1937 member of the Bailey chain); and jobs/namier's complete search of every held order text (30,725 texts for 14,913 census orders, checked 2026-10-28) for the exempted person's full name, which found every later order in this person's exemption chain that the project holds (listed as later events) and nothing else. That name search replaces the per-order surname search a producer previously ran by hand (compare the X1 pilot's EO 5881). It covers only held texts: the person's actual separation or death date is not in any held source and is not asserted.
retirement:statute: Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404; the Economy Act), which bars continued civilian service past the retirement age unless the President exempts the person by Executive order. Each order in this family recites that section. No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before the order's stated end date, and the later orders in the same chain (held texts, cited by number in the claim's later events) show the President still granting such exemptions after the earlier order's end, so the statutory scheme the exemption operates against continued through the stated date.
